anna_sales: quick escalation — POC with bank failing on Private endpoint, intermittent 502s and 'handshake failure'. Need network + security input tonight before demo.
kevin_se: are they using site-to-site IPsec to our colo?
anna_sales: yes. Customer firewall team reports fragmented certs in tcpdump.
otmar_neteng: likely MTU/MSS issues on the IPsec tunnel. Ask them to run:
openssl s_client -connect 10.20.30.40:443 -servername poc.bank.example -showcerts
ping -M do -s 1400 <peer-ip>
Quick mitigation: apply MSS clamp or set tunnel MTU to 1400. Example iptables rule: `iptables -t mangle -A FORWARD -p tcp --tcp-flags SYN,RST SYN -j TCPMSS --clamp-mss-to-pmtu`.
kevin_se: also confirm their perimeter does not perform TLS interception and preserves SNI/ClientHello. If they terminate TLS we need a different deployment model.
lucy_security: for the security questionnaire please request: confirmation that customer-managed edge does not do TLS MITM and that private keys remain in customer's HSM. We'll provide a short statement once confirmed.
anna_sales: they applied MSS clamp and re-ran health check -> now returns HTTP/200 consistently. Customer asks for a short SOC-friendly explanation to attach to their ticket.
lucy_security: I'll draft a 2-line blurb: "Root cause: MTU/MSS on customer IPsec caused TLS handshake fragments to be dropped by a middlebox. Mitigation: clamp MSS or set tunnel MTU to 1400; ensure TLS is end-to-end without interception for Private deployments."
billing_bot: quote request Q-8001 created for a 3-week dedicated pod, assigned to finance.
anna_sales: thanks all — blocker resolved. I'll send SOC note and follow up on pricing and legal confirmation.
